top.title: Customs hands over seized LPG laden truck to NMDPRA in Calabar
top.description: …auctions seized PMS worth N6.1million By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The Nigeria Customs Service, through Operation Whirlwind, on Friday handed over an intercepted truck conveying diverted Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) to the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA). The truck, with registration number KAM 663 XA, was handed over at the Customs House, Calabar. It was intercepted by operatives of the Operation Whirlwind Zone C team, Calabar Axis. The National Coordinator of Operation Whirlwind, Drputy Comptroller of Cutsoms , Mahmood Bello Esq , performed the handover on the directive of the Comptroller-General of Customs, Bashir Adewale Adeniyi. Bello said the handover demonstrated the importance of cooperation between government agencies. “The formal handover to NMDPRA further demonstrates the importance of inter-agency cooperation in ensuring appropriate regulatory action and accountability,” he said. He described the diversion and smuggling of petroleum products as a threat to the country’s economy . “The illegal diversion and smuggling of petroleum products remain serious threats to our national economy, energy security and public interest,” he said. Speaking earlier , the Acting Customs Area Controller, Cross River/Calabar Free Trade Zone/Akwa Ibom Area Command, Nkiruka Nwalla said the exercise showed the Service’s resolve to enforce petroleum regulations. “The formal handover of this LPG tanker to the NMDPRA further demonstrates the importance of inter-agency collaboration in ensuring regulatory compliance and accountability in the petroleum sector,” she said. The Service also publicly auctioned 6,125 litres of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS), packed in 245 jerrycans of 25 litres each. The fuel was seized at Ikang Road (Bakassi), Ibaka and Mfum. Its Duty Paid Value is N6,125,000. Bello said the auction followed established procedures and was meant to ensure transparency, particularly because seized petroleum products are volatile and must be disposed of promptly. Bello said intelligence reports indicated that attempts to divert and smuggle PMS and other products could increase during the festive season. He directed all commanders to raise operational readiness and strengthen surveillance around known flashpoints. He also said Operation Whirlwind would not stop at seizures adding that they must identify offenders and prosecute them. “Our mandate goes beyond making seizures; we must ensure that identified offenders are properly investigated and prosecuted,” he said. Bello, the newly appointed National Coordinator, pledged purposeful leadership and a more intelligence-driven approach. “We will ensure that economic saboteurs find no refuge anywhere within our operational environment,” he added. top.title: ‘No s***, Sherlock’: Michael Vaughan takes brutal dig as Usman Khawaja reopens Australia's ball-tampering scandal
top.description: Former England captain Michael Vaughan has reacted sarcastically to the fresh revelations surrounding Australia's infamous 2018 ball-tampering scandal, suggesting that Usman Khawaja's claims about widespread knowledge within the team were hardly surprising. Khawaja has reignited the 'Sandpapergate' controversy through excerpts from his upcoming autobiography, claiming that discussions about tampering with the ball were much more widespread during Australia's 2018 tour of South Africa than Cricket Australia's investigation had established. Taking to X, Vaughan took a dig at the revelations, suggesting that the latest claims merely confirmed what many had suspected all along. He also questioned why the issue was being revisited nearly eight years after the scandal and called for everyone to move on. "So we finally now know the most hidden secret in the game … all the Aussie team knew about the sandpaper … 8 yrs later it all comes out … no shit Sherlock … now can we just move on …" Vaughan posted. The controversy dates back to the third Test between Australia and South Africa in Cape Town in March 2018, when Cameron Bancroft was caught using sandpaper to rough up the ball. The incident triggered a major crisis for Australian cricket and resulted in lengthy suspensions for Steve Smith, David Warner and Bancroft. Cricket Australia's investigation at the time concluded that prior knowledge of the ball-tampering plan was limited to the three players. Head coach Darren Lehmann was cleared of direct involvement but resigned shortly after the series. However, Khawaja has now claimed that conversations about roughing up the ball, including through the use of sandpaper, took place openly within the team. "It was all of us," the former Australia batter said in his autobiography, according to the Sydney Morning Herald. Khawaja, who was cleared of wrongdoing during the original investigation, also described the conversations as "open, lighthearted discussions" and maintained that awareness of the subject extended beyond just the batters, bowlers or coaching staff. Cricket Australia has stood by its original investigation, insisting that all relevant information presented to the governing body had been considered. It also maintained that individuals still had the opportunity to provide any additional information. Australia captain Pat Cummins, who featured in the Cape Town Test, had earlier played down suggestions that Khawaja's autobiography would trigger further fallout from the scandal. Australia and South Africa have since faced each other again in a Test series, with the visitors returning to the country last month for the first time since the 2018 controversy. top.title: Fascinating stats! How often your Bundesliga club plays in prime time
top.description: Fascinating stats! How often your Bundesliga club plays in prime time As of Thursday, exact kickoff times have been set for every match in the first half of the Bundesliga season. That means we can now say precisely how often each team will play at which times and, most importantly, on which days. A glance at the figures makes one thing immediately clear: "smaller" clubs play far more often at 3:30 p.m. on Saturday afternoons—the traditional Bundesliga prime-time slot—than the country's big, historic clubs. It is no coincidence that Paderborn (14) and Elversberg (11), two newly promoted sides without much top-flight history, feature in the top three of the Saturday crowd. The reason—apart from some clubs' involvement in European competitions—is obvious: teams that do not generate huge TV interest are much easier to "hide" in the simultaneous-match coverage than in standalone broadcasts. The simultaneous-match format, with its many goals and dramatic twists, remains as popular as ever, while a standalone match between, say, Paderborn and Elversberg would presumably attract far less interest. Clubs like Bayern Munich are the losers in this development—or, more precisely, their fans are. Bayern will play on a Saturday afternoon just three times during the first half of the season, and not once at home. top.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, 15, all set to captain Bihar in Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy as selectors look for fresh direction
top.description: KOLKATA: At 15, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is set for his first assignment as Bihar’s senior team captain, with the selectors handing the teenage batting sensation the reins for the upcoming Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy. The move underlines their faith in his leadership potential as Bihar seek a turnaround after losing all four of their opening Ranji Trophy matches. Sakibul Gani led Bihar in the first three Ranji games before Mangal Mahrour took over against Goa, but neither captain could arrest the slide. The BCCI-appointed selection committee, headed by Harvinder Singh, has now turned to Vaibhav, with Suraj Kashyap named his deputy for the domestic T20 tournament. The decision by the selection committee, led by chief selector Harvinder Singh and comprising Amitabh Vijayvargiya and S Sarath, marks another significant step in Vaibhav’s rapid rise. Having represented Rajasthan Royals in the IPL and made his India debut in T20Is, the teenager has quickly established himself as one of the country’s most exciting batting prospects. His recent international exploits included a 45 off 19 balls against New Zealand in the third T20I, where he shared a record-breaking opening stand with Abhishek Sharma. Vaibhav has also had a taste of leadership at the zonal level. Named vice-captain of the Ishan Kishan-led East Zone side, he briefly took charge during the Duleep Trophy semifinal when Kishan left the field with a finger injury. During that spell, he also successfully executed a DRS call. However, his rapid elevation to positions of responsibility comes amid questions about the need to balance expectations with his development. Sachin Tendulkar recently advocated giving Vaibhav more opportunities in red-ball cricket to help him grow as a complete cricketer, while cautioning against placing excessive responsibility on his young shoulders too early. The selectors, though, appear to have a different assessment, with the Bihar captaincy adding another responsibility to Vaibhav’s expanding portfolio. BCA president Harsh Vardhan said the appointment would provide the youngster another opportunity to develop as a leader. “Vaibhav has already demonstrated tremendous talent, confidence and maturity at a young age, and this responsibility will provide him with another opportunity to grow as a cricketer and leader,” he said. Bihar begin their SMAT campaign in Indore on Nov 14. The 17-member squad also includes Mahrour and Sunrisers Hyderabad pacer Shakib Hussain, whose availability will depend on fitness assessments after the first two matches. Singh and Vijayvargiya will be present in Indore to watch Bihar’s matches. top.title: Arsenal youth trains with first-team amid senior international call-up
top.description: Arsenal youth trains with first-team amid senior international call-up Arsenal youngster James Scanlon is having a good week, receiving call-ups to train with the Gunners first-team and to play with Gibraltar over the international break. Photo via Scanlon on Instagram Ahead of Arsenal’s game against Hull City on Saturday, 20-year-old winger James Scanlon was spotted training with Mikel Arteta’s senior side on Friday. Arsenal are obviously a little low on wingers at the moment, with Bukayo Saka out of action through injury and Max Dowman suspended. With Scanlon scoring three goals and assisting one in his first five Premier League 2 appearances for the Gunners, he’s earned a chance in training. But that wasn’t the only boost for the former Manchester United winger this week, as he’s also been called up to the Gibraltar senior squad for the November break. Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images The international call-up isn’t surprising, as Scanlon has already made 28 appearances for Gibraltar in his young career. In fact, Scanlon is currently the team’s second-top scorer of all time, with six goals. He only trails retired international Liam Walker , who scored eight during his international career. The Arsenal man will get an opportunity to add to his total in Nations League fixtures away to Andorra and at home to Malta over the upcoming break. Photo by Carsten Harz/Getty Images With all that being said, it’s unlikely Scanlon receives a call-up for the Arsenal first-team squad for Saturday afternoon’s match against Hull City. Though Arsenal are a little light in forward areas, Saka and Dowman are actually the only players in the entire senior squad expected to miss the game. Everyone else should be available, meaning very limited bench spaces for youth players, if any. Photo by Carsten Harz/Getty Images

On paper, another 46-13 victory over Silver Bluff to open the postseason looked dominant. Defense played really well at times. We’ve just got to keep working on being as consistent as we can be.” The standards are high for Strom Thurmond football, and as it fights to defend last year's state title, it will need to widen the gap on the scoreboard against more difficult opponents. But for Silver Bluff, despite the loss, it’s a sign of what may come for the future of a young program in head coach Lemuel Lackey’s first season. While it was an uphill battle for the Bulldogs, they were able to put together some scoring drives and make some plays on defense to keep the Rebels on their toes. “ I am so optimistic about this group, just simply because we had a lot of guys that were just out there trying to scrap and play and do some good things,” he said. “We grew up as the season went on, and we have a lot of young kids out there, and it is a tremendous effort on their part. top.description: NHS staff drafted into a helpline after colleagues' health data was exposed online faced distressed callers, safeguarding concerns, and a "serious emotional impact," a review has found. The report [PDF] comes almost exactly a year after the Royal Cornwall Hospitals NHS Trust disclosed a data breach affecting 8,003 people, including current and former trust staff and non-trust workers. A member of the public discovered the exposure in November 2025. An Excel workbook published in response to a Freedom of Information request in February 2023 retained underlying sickness absence records that users could reveal through its pivot tables. Staff assigned to the helpline described difficult calls involving shouting, anger, and distress. Particularly difficult calls involved people distressed by the sensitivity of the disclosures or potentially in danger from domestic abuse. Call handlers said they had to make safeguarding assessments without training or an established process. "Such occurrences of anger or distress were not infrequent, and this reflected the heightened emotions and distress experienced by callers to varying degrees due to the breach," the review noted. "This placed significant emotional burden on individuals working in the contact center, who were not prepared or provided support on how to deal with those." Members of the trust's clinical governance team were told just a day beforehand that they would staff the helpline. Despite their experience dealing with patient trauma, they received little preparation for the calls that followed. "The staff working in the call centers had a short training session and then the calls started coming in within minutes of the team being set up," the review noted. "Some staff had not finished reading the pre-prepared script which had arrived only 30 minutes before the center went live." Most call handlers only learned that their own data had been exposed while already working on the helpline, sometimes minutes before supporting others affected. Call handlers also said they had little choice about taking on the work and were expected to maintain their usual duties alongside it. The review stated that some staff members gave up weekends and worked long past their scheduled hours to meet the demands of both roles. "It's typical NHS, it runs on goodwill," one staffer told the team that compiled the report. The call center was only supposed to run for two weeks in December 2025, but due to the volume of calls, it was eventually stood down after 11 weeks, in February 2026. According to officials speaking at a trust board meeting on Thursday, the review and its findings have since been circulated among staff, and published online. How the spreadsheet slipped through Responding to a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request thought to be from a journalist researching a story about stress in the NHS, the Royal Cornwall Hospitals NHS Trust uploaded a spreadsheet to its public FOI Disclosure log in February 2023. top.description: Stafford Rangers manager Graham Deakin stepped up from his role as coach to take over at Marston Road in February - and save his side from the drop [Stafford Rangers FC] Stafford Rangers go into Sunday's FA Cup first-round tie with promotion-chasing League Two side Grimsby Town as very much the underdogs. They are the lowest-ranked side left in this year's competition. Second in the Northern Premier League West Division, the eighth-tier club will be up against a team from four levels higher - currently standing sixth in League Two. Skip back 50 years and Rangers were ruling the roost in non-league football. Three times they went to Wembley, twice winning the FA Trophy, in 1972 and 1979, under the command of Roy Chapman, father of Leeds United title winner and former Stoke City striker Lee. And, in between, they also reached the fourth round of the FA Cup. Despite being founder members of non-league football's first 'fifth division', the Alliance Premier League, when it launched in 1979, it then all fizzled out as the club went into decline. The average weekly crowds of up to 4,000 dropped off, finances suffered and Rangers lost their way. From the archives: Stafford Rangers on BBC Radio Stoke Rangers did win back their place in the fifth tier briefly in 2006, under Stafford-born former Wolves and Stoke midfielder Phil Robinson. But that lasted just two seasons and he had departed before they went back down again under Wolves legend Steve Bull in 2008. Now Rangers are back up and fighting again - and this cup run has been a major catalyst, encapsulated by the 5-0 fourth qualifying round replay win over Gateshead which got them to this stage. "The feeling we have around the club is one of anticipation," chief executive David Smith told BBC Radio Stoke. "The place is buzzing. "There's people everywhere working, trying to get the ground ready – to make it the way we want to be. "It's quite a challenge for us, to be live on TV on Sunday lunchtime. But the staff have put in many hours of service to be match ready. We've already had three full houses here of 3,000 plus crowds, so we're almost getting used to it." The club's assistant manager, Alfie Marsden, works in a chip shop by day. top.title: Brazil face North Korea seeking first U17 Women's World Cup medal
top.description: Brazil face North Korea seeking first U17 Women's World Cup medal Brazil’s U-17 women’s national team faces another decisive test this Saturday (7). Led by head coach Rilany Silva, the team takes on North Korea at 12 p.m. (Brasília time) in the third-place match of the U-17 Women’s World Cup at the Mohammed VI Women’s Football Complex in Salé, Morocco. At stake is the chance to claim Brazil’s first-ever medal in the competition. After reaching the semifinals for the second consecutive year, the Seleção hopes to turn its campaign into a historic achievement and finish the World Cup among the top three teams on the planet. The match also offers an opportunity to overcome an opponent Brazil has faced in two previous editions of the U-17 World Cup. So far, the Asian side holds the advantage, having won both previous encounters. Goalkeeper Nathy saves two penalties in the quarterfinal against Poland at the U-17 World Cup in Morocco Credits: Joern Pollex / FIFA World Cup head-to-head record Brazil and North Korea first met in the group stage of the 2016 edition. On that occasion, the North Koreans won 1–0. The teams met again in the semifinal of the 2025 World Cup. Once again, North Korea came out on top, this time winning 2–0 to advance to the final. That gives the Asian side two wins in two matches, with three goals scored and none conceded. Now, in a new chapter of this history, Brazil will have the chance to claim its first victory over North Korea at a U-17 World Cup and, most importantly, secure a place on the podium. Helena scores both goals in Brazil’s quarterfinal win over China at the U-17 World Cup Credits: Fabio Souza / CBF The road to the bronze-medal match Brazil reached the semifinals after a strong campaign. In the group stage, Brazil beat Canada 6–2, drew 3–3 with Ghana and defeated Norway 3–0 to secure top spot in Group C. In the round of 16, the Seleção delivered another thrilling encounter. After drawing 3–3 with Poland in regulation time, Brazil won the penalty shootout 8–7. Next, in the quarterfinals, the team came from behind to beat China 2–1, securing a place among the tournament’s final four. In the semifinal, however, Brazil lost 3–1 to Nigeria. North Korea, meanwhile, advanced as Group B winners after victories over Puerto Rico and Poland and a defeat to Nigeria. In the knockout stage, the team eliminated Morocco in the round of 16 and the United States in the quarterfinals. In the semifinal, North Korea lost to Japan on penalties after a draw in regulation time. top.description: Napoli President De Laurentiis puts temporary trust in Allegri after face-to-face talks Napoli President Aurelio De Laurentiis has put his trust in head coach Massimiliano Allegri for the time being following a round of crisis talks at the training ground on Saturday, which came after a troubling start to the 2026-27 season that has brought seven defeats from the first 14 matches. Allegri still has De Laurentiis’s trust after Napoli crisis talks It’s fair to say that Napoli have not quite got going since Allegri replaced Antonio Conte as head coach over the summer. They find themselves in eighth place in Serie A, already 14 points behind the league leaders after 10 matches, and are at serious risk of missing out on qualification to the Champions League knock-out rounds after losing three of their first four games in Europe in 2026-27. There have also been reports towards the end of the week suggesting that there is a divided dressing room in Naples , that some players are too individualistic and that others have broken off into small cliques. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) Napoli are now heading into another tough test on Sunday, at home against the Serie A leaders Lazio, who have won all five of their away matches in the league so far this season. top.title: Struggling star set to return to Liverpool in January – Report
top.description: Struggling star set to return to Liverpool in January – Report Harvey Elliott and Valencia Loan Struggles Could Open Door to Liverpool Return in January Harvey Elliott’s difficult start at Valencia is increasingly pointing towards a possible early return to Liverpool, with adaptation to LaLiga emerging as a central issue in the club’s summer recruitment. According to Plaza Deportivo , Valencia are assessing whether several signings have settled as hoped, and Elliott’s situation is firmly part of that conversation. The broader picture at Valencia appears to be one of underwhelming integration. The report outlines how the jump into Spanish football has hit a number of arrivals, and Elliott is among those yet to establish momentum. Minutes have been limited, influence has been minimal and, as the weeks have passed, there has been no real sense of a breakthrough building. Valencia loan under growing scrutiny For Liverpool, this is the sort of development that warrants close monitoring well before the January window opens. Elliott’s move was meant to provide rhythm, continuity and the chance to rebuild after a previous loan spell that offered very little in competitive terms. Instead, there is a risk that another season drifts by without the attacking midfielder gaining the foothold his career needs. The concern here is practical as much as strategic. A young player who needs games cannot afford another six months on the fringes. Liverpool will know that a stagnant loan helps nobody, not the player, not the parent club and not the market value attached to a footballer who still has obvious technical quality. Photo: IMAGO Harvey Elliott facing another stalled season The key issue appears to be adaptation. Valencia’s recruitment has not landed smoothly, and Elliott’s profile may simply not be aligning with the demands currently being placed upon him. That does not automatically make the move a failure in football terms, but it does raise a serious question over whether staying until the end of the campaign serves any meaningful purpose. If Valencia decide that a change is required, Liverpool may not need much convincing to sanction an early recall. Clubs are usually reluctant to cut short temporary deals unless the circumstances are clear, yet this feels like a case where clarity is arriving quickly. Elliott needs an environment where he is trusted, selected and developed with consistency. January transfer decision could suit all parties An early return would not necessarily resolve everything immediately. Liverpool would still need to determine whether Elliott remains as squad depth, moves again on loan or is positioned for a more permanent solution. But bringing him back at least restores control over a situation that currently appears to be slipping away. There is also a wider lesson in this. top.title: Arsenal Starting XI vs Hull City: Confirmed Team News and Predicted Lineup
top.description: Arsenal Starting XI vs Hull City: Confirmed Team News and Predicted Lineup Arsenal vs Hull: William Saliba Return Nears as Arteta Weighs Selection Against Hull Arsenal head into Saturday’s Premier League meeting with Hull at the Emirates Stadium with one obvious talking point, William Saliba is finally close to playing again. The defender has not featured at all this season after a back injury, a problem that worsened during the World Cup. Now he is back in the frame. He was on the bench in midweek against Slavia Prague and, barring a setback, should be in Mikel Arteta’s squad again here. The expectation is simple, Arsenal will not take risks. A start would be a surprise, a short run-out from the bench feels far more realistic if the match allows it. Saliba Boost for Arsenal Defence That matters because Arsenal have had to manage resources carefully. Ezri Konsa went off in Prague with a knee issue, but the concern appears minimal. Arteta shut that down quickly, saying: “Yeah, he’s fine. He was feeling much better today. We took him out for a precaution but yesterday and today he’s feeling good.” Riccardo Calafiori, rested completely in the 2-1 win over Slavia Prague, should return at left-back. Gabriel remains the certainty in central defence, while Jurrien Timber is expected to continue on the right. Photo IMAGO Midfield Shape Looks Straightforward In midfield, this looks uncomplicated. Bruno Guimaraes did not play in Europe and should come straight back in alongside Declan Rice. Arsenal need control, tempo and security in possession, and that pairing gives them all three. Further forward, Martin Odegaard remains the central creative hub. On the right, Noni Madueke has done enough to keep his place. With Bukayo Saka injured and Max Dowman suspended for two league matches, there is no real debate there. Arteta Faces Attacking Decision The left side is less clear. Christos Tzolis looked lively against Liverpool, while Eberechi Eze strengthened his case in midweek. Arteta has a genuine choice there, one based on profile rather than form alone. Up front, Kai Havertz may get the nod despite Viktor Gyokeres delivering a goal and an assist last time out. That is the sort of call managers make when balancing rhythm, opposition and workload. Predicted Arsenal XI vs Hull, 4-2-3-1: Raya, Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori, Rice, Guimaraes, Madueke, Odegaard, Tzolis, Havertz. Kick-off is 3pm GMT on Saturday November 7, 2026, at the Emirates Stadium.

nigeria.title: Customs hands over seized LPG laden truck to NMDPRA in Calabar
nigeria.description: …auctions seized PMS worth N6.1million By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The Nigeria Customs Service, through Operation Whirlwind, on Friday handed over an intercepted truck conveying diverted Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) to the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA). The truck, with registration number KAM 663 XA, was handed over at the Customs House, Calabar. It was intercepted by operatives of the Operation Whirlwind Zone C team, Calabar Axis. The National Coordinator of Operation Whirlwind, Drputy Comptroller of Cutsoms , Mahmood Bello Esq , performed the handover on the directive of the Comptroller-General of Customs, Bashir Adewale Adeniyi. Bello said the handover demonstrated the importance of cooperation between government agencies. “The formal handover to NMDPRA further demonstrates the importance of inter-agency cooperation in ensuring appropriate regulatory action and accountability,” he said. He described the diversion and smuggling of petroleum products as a threat to the country’s economy . “The illegal diversion and smuggling of petroleum products remain serious threats to our national economy, energy security and public interest,” he said. Speaking earlier , the Acting Customs Area Controller, Cross River/Calabar Free Trade Zone/Akwa Ibom Area Command, Nkiruka Nwalla said the exercise showed the Service’s resolve to enforce petroleum regulations. “The formal handover of this LPG tanker to the NMDPRA further demonstrates the importance of inter-agency collaboration in ensuring regulatory compliance and accountability in the petroleum sector,” she said. The Service also publicly auctioned 6,125 litres of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS), packed in 245 jerrycans of 25 litres each. The fuel was seized at Ikang Road (Bakassi), Ibaka and Mfum. Its Duty Paid Value is N6,125,000. Bello said the auction followed established procedures and was meant to ensure transparency, particularly because seized petroleum products are volatile and must be disposed of promptly. Bello said intelligence reports indicated that attempts to divert and smuggle PMS and other products could increase during the festive season. He directed all commanders to raise operational readiness and strengthen surveillance around known flashpoints. He also said Operation Whirlwind would not stop at seizures adding that they must identify offenders and prosecute them. “Our mandate goes beyond making seizures; we must ensure that identified offenders are properly investigated and prosecuted,” he said. Bello, the newly appointed National Coordinator, pledged purposeful leadership and a more intelligence-driven approach. “We will ensure that economic saboteurs find no refuge anywhere within our operational environment,” he added. nigeria.title: FIFA U-17 WWC Final: Nigeria vs Japan – date, time and where to watch
nigeria.description: Nigeria’s Flamingos will face Japan in the final of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco on Saturday, November 7, as they seek to make history by winning their first title. The final, which will be the 52nd and last match of the tournament, will kick off at 7:30 p.m. Nigerian time at the Mohammed VI Football Complex, Pitch 3, in Rabat. The encounter will be the first meeting between Nigeria and Japan at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup and the first time the two countries face each other in a global final. Where to watch Nigeria vs Japan Football fans can watch the final live and for free through FIFA+, with streaming available via DAZN. How Nigeria reached the final Nigeria’s campaign in Morocco did not begin as expected, as the Flamingos suffered a 2-1 defeat to Poland in their opening group match. They subsequently recorded a narrow victory over Puerto Rico before producing one of the tournament’s biggest upsets by defeating defending champions DPR Korea 3-1. The Nigerian side built on that result with victories over Mexico and Venezuela before overcoming Brazil in the semi-finals to secure a historic place in the final. Queen Joseph was particularly impressive against Brazil, scoring a goal and providing an assist to help Nigeria reach their maiden U-17 Women’s World Cup final. Nigeria are the first African country to reach the final of the competition. How Japan reached the final Japan, meanwhile, have been impressive throughout the tournament, winning all their group-stage matches without conceding a goal. Although they fell behind against Kenya in the round of 16, Sadayoshi Shirai’s team recovered to secure a 3-1 victory. They subsequently edged Ghana to reach the semi-finals, where they faced DPR Korea. Japan came from behind in the closing stages, benefiting from a late own goal before winning the contest through a penalty shootout to book their place in a fourth U-17 Women’s World Cup final. Players to watch For Japan, Mei Hanashiro will be one of the players Nigeria must watch closely. The forward has scored four goals and provided one assist at the tournament, making her one of the team’s leading attacking threats. Nigeria will look to Queen Joseph, whose pace and attacking quality have made her one of the standout players of the competition. Her goal and assist against Brazil underlined her importance to the Flamingos’ title ambitions. What the coaches and captains said Japan coach Sadayoshi Shirai said his team were determined to complete their campaign by winning the trophy. “We don’t want to stop here. We’ll continue moving forward, prepare as well as we can for the final, and give everything we have to become world champions.” Japan captain Honoka Yotsumoto also expressed confidence ahead of the encounter. “We’ve managed to overcome barriers that had held us back for so long, one step at a time – that has given us a lot of confidence. Now we have just one more match to win, and we’re determined to make history.” Nigeria

nigeria.title: ‎APC explains omission of ex-Jigawa governor Badaru from campaign council
nigeria.description: By Muhammad Inuwa, DUTSE ‎The All Progressives Congress, APC, in Jigawa State has explained why former governor and ex-Minister of Defence, Muhammad Badaru Abubakar, was not included in the party’s recently-announced governorship campaign council. Jigawa State House of Assembly’ Speaker, Haruna Aliyu Dangyatin, gave the explanation while responding to questions from journalists over Badaru’s absence from the list. ‎Dangyatin said Badaru, being a prominent national political figure, has broader responsibilities at the national level ahead of the 2027 general elections. ‎According to him, assigning the former governor to the state governorship campaign council would limit his ability to contribute to the party’s campaign efforts at the national and regional levels. ‎“Including the former governor in the governorship campaign council is like tying him down and restricting him from contributing to the party’s victory,” the Speaker said. ‎He added that Badaru currently serves as the Director-General of Arewa for Asiwaju, a position that requires him to coordinate political activities across the North and the country. ‎“The former governor is the Director-General of Arewa for Asiwaju. He is dealing with the entire region and the country,” Dangyatin stated. ‎The Speaker, however, dismissed speculations that Badaru’s exclusion from the campaign council was connected to internal divisions within the Jigawa APC. ‎He maintained that the party had no disagreement with the former governor, insisting that the APC in the state remained united. ‎Dangyatin urged party supporters to disregard what he described as rumours and propaganda surrounding Badaru’s omission and instead focus on mobilising support for the party ahead of the 2027 general elections. nigeria.title: Troops rescue three female kidnap victims in Plateau
nigeria.description: By Golok Nanmwa, JOS Troops of Operation Enduring Peace (OPEP) have rescued three female kidnap victims unharmed after confronting their abductors at Makundang village, Mangor District, in Bokkos Local Government Area of Plateau State. The victims were rescued following a search-and-rescue operation launched by troops of Sector 5 of OPEP after receiving a distress report about a kidnapping incident at about 8:50 p.m. on November 5, 2026. Security sources told newsmen that the troops swiftly mobilised to the area and established contact with the kidnappers, who reportedly abandoned their victims and fled into the surrounding bush following pressure from the security personnel. The rescued victims were identified as Miss Fatigi Aguna, 19; Lovina Bawa, 18; and Barsheba Appolos, 18. The sources said all three victims were rescued unhurt and subsequently reunited with their families. They added that troops had intensified efforts to track down and apprehend the fleeing kidnappers, assuring residents that security operations were ongoing to prevent further criminal activities in the area. Confirming the development on Saturday, the spokesperson for Operation Enduring Peace, Captain Polycarp Chinonso Oteh, said the operation was part of ongoing efforts by security personnel to protect lives and property across the Joint Operations Area. Oteh appreciated residents for their cooperation with security agencies and appealed for sustained support through the provision of credible and timely information to assist security operatives in restoring lasting peace in the area. He urged members of the public to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious movements and activities to security agencies, noting that public cooperation remained vital to the success of ongoing operations. nigeria.title: 2027: Why is Obi facing attacks despite finishing third in 2023? – Utomi
nigeria.description: Professor of Political Economy, Pat Utomi, has questioned the criticism directed at former Anambra State Governor and Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, Peter Obi, asking why he continues to face attacks despite finishing third in the 2023 presidential election. Utomi raised the question in a post on his verified X handle on Saturday, saying the level of hostility towards Obi deserved an explanation. “There is no convincing explanation for why a candidate who finished third in the 2023 presidential election attracts this level of hostility from all directions. “The intensity of the attacks raises questions that Nigerians deserve answers to. Perhaps one day, we will finally understand what really happened in 2023,” Utomi wrote. Although Utomi did not mention any individual or political party in his post, his comments came after criticism from President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and his vice, Kashim Shettima, including the senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole. Recall that Tinubu took a swipe at Obi at the All Progressives Congress (APC) rally held at the Godswill Akpabio Stadium in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, on Friday, accusing the former Anambra governor of failing to tackle erosion during his time in office while contrasting it with his own record as Lagos State governor. “He’s in one party; they called NDC, who is running for president; he ran away from erosion in Anambra State. He could not confront erosion,” Tinubu said. “I, Bola Ahmed Tinubu, confronted the Atlantic Ocean; I tamed it for you. Umo Eno confronted the erosion in Akwa Ibom, and it’s working for you.” Similarly, Shettima at the same event accused Obi of losing the goodwill he previously enjoyed among Nigerians, alleging that the NDC candidate had relied on false claims and misleading statistics. “And clearly this gentle man has run himself out of this race with his lies and bogus statistics. We warned him that he’ll get to that. “Peter Obi has clearly messed up and squandered away his goodwill; he no longer excites when he speaks these days. He draws suspicions; it’s too bad for him.” Oshiomhole, during an appearance on Channels TV Politics Today on Thursday, described the Obi as a trader who has failed to present an alternative to Tinubu’s policies ahead of the 2027 general election. “Peter Obi has not offered any alternative. nigeria.title: Naira Would Have Been Worthless Without Economic Reforms, Tinubu Tells Nigerians
nigeria.description: President Bola Tinubu has defended his administration’s economic reforms, saying the naira would have become worthless if his government had failed to take decisive action to remove the fuel subsidy upon assuming office. He made the remarks at a state reception held in his honour at the newly constructed Banquet Hall of ARISE Palm Resort in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, following the APC rally at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium. Tinubu said his administration inherited an economy in which 27 of the country’s 36 state governors were unable to meet their salary obligations, let alone pay pensions and gratuities. “When I took over, 27 governors out of 36 of this country were unable to pay salary obligation, not to talk of pension and gratuity. Today I stand before you able to say we are out of that tunnel. I can beat my chest to say we are out of the greatest despair, the dark tunnel of uncertainty and the calamity of possible bankruptcy.” Tinubu speaking at a state reception held in his honour at the newly constructed Banquet Hall of ARISE Palm Resort in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, following the APC rally at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, on Friday, November 6, 2026. Defending the decisions taken by his government, the President said: “By now, if we didn’t take a decision, the day I took over, we would use wheelbarrows to move our naira. Because it would have been valueless, nothing.” He added that the exchange rate was about ₦1,300 to the dollar, arguing that the currency had retained some value because of the decisions his administration took. President Tinubu insisted that his administration would not reverse its decision to end the policy. Using the biblical account of Moses and the Israelites’ departure from Egypt, he said Nigeria must continue moving forward, stating: “Nigeria will never go back to the subsidy.” “We are talking of $1,300 now to a dollar. Because it still has pocketable value. If we had left it, it would have been a wheelbarrow when you go to a tomato market. Tehran has sought to limit traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption. nigeria.title: Houston mayor limits immigration agents cooperation by police after Democratic victory
nigeria.description: The mayor of Houston, Texas announced Friday that the city’s police department will limit its cooperation with federal immigration agents after Democrats swept midterm elections this week. The so-called “blue tsunami” ousted Republican Governor Greg Abbott, a close Texas ally of US President Donald Trump, who has cracked down on immigration with raids conducted by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents since returning to office last year. Abbott had threatened in April to revoke $110 million in public safety funding from Houston if city officials didn’t walk back a similar measure earlier this year, and city officials complied. He lost reelection on Tuesday and will be replaced by Democrat Gina Hinojosa, the first Latina woman elected governor of Texas. Now, Houston Mayor John Whitmire has signed an executive order instructing Houston police to not contact ICE agents when a person is detained for nonviolent offenses, like a traffic stop. “It’s to reduce the fear and anxiety, not just in some of our communities but across Houston,” Whitmire said during a press conference announcing the change. The 77-year-old mayor acknowledged that the change could bring some political risks but said he was ready to meet them, as Abbott and other Republicans remain in power until January. ICE released a statement on X reacting to the change, writing: “Watching child porn and selling heroin are classified as ‘nonviolent offenses’ by the way.” “This is the Mayor of Houston directly advocating for policies that protect some of the worst criminals in America,” it added. According to the Prison Policy Initiative, a nonpartisan think tank, Texas has had more arrests carried out by ICE agents during Trump’s second term than any other state, with almost 137,000 recorded as of August 2026. Texas is also the state with the highest number of ICE detainees in the US, with over 16,000 held at various facilities — more than double the amount held in the second highest state, Louisiana — according to Syracuse University’s Transactional Records Access Clearinghouse. nigeria.title: Nigeria Presides Over Key UN Election
nigeria.description: Nigeria has presided over key elections at the United Nations General Assembly’s Fifth Committee, with Mauritania and Israel emerging as beneficiaries of two significant appointments during the 81st Session of the General Assembly. The elections, conducted under the chairmanship of Nigeria’s permanent representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Jimoh Ibrahim, saw C.D. Mohammed of Mauritania recommended as Chair of the International Civil Service Commission, while Israel’s candidate, Shai Mazai, secured a place on the Independent Audit Advisory Committee. In a demonstration of transparency in the electoral process, Ambassador Ibrahim directed that the ballot boxes be opened before voting commenced, allowing delegates to verify the boxes ahead of the collection of ballots. In the contest for the chairmanship of the International Civil Service Commission, C.D. Mohammed of Mauritania secured 102 votes, defeating Mrs. Maria of Zimbabwe, who polled 82 votes. Having obtained the required majority of 93 votes, Mohammed was recommended by the Fifth Committee to the General Assembly for designation as Chair of the International Civil Service Commission for a four-year term beginning January 1, 2027. In another significant outcome, Israel’s Mr. Shai Mazai secured 134 votes to emerge as the recommended candidate from the Group of Western European and Other States to the Independent Audit Advisory Committee. The Fifth Committee subsequently recommended his appointment to the committee for a three-year term, also beginning January 1, 2027. The elections formed part of the Committee’s consideration of Agenda Item 119, which covers appointments to fill vacancies in subsidiary organs and other appointments. Other bodies considered during the exercise included the Advisory Committee on Administrative and Budgetary Questions, the Committee on Contributions and the Investment Committee, alongside the International Civil Service Commission and the Independent Audit Advisory Committee. The Fifth Committee, chaired by Ambassador Jimoh Ibrahim, also recommended candidates from other regional groups to the International Civil Service Commission through acclamation, following the absence of contested nominations for the respective seats. At the conclusion of the exercise, Ambassador Ibrahim commended delegates for their patience, cooperation and commitment throughout the electoral process. He also congratulated those recommended for appointment and urged them to uphold the integrity of the Fifth Committee while discharging their responsibilities. The Nigerian diplomat equally acknowledged the contributions of the tellers and officials nominated by Member States to supervise the electoral process. Ambassador Ibrahim subsequently declared the Committee’s consideration of Agenda Item 119 concluded and requested the Rapporteur to communicate its decisions to the General Assembly for further action. Read Also: Iran warns of wider war if US attacks after Trump election rout A State Department program, Rewards for Justice, “is offering a reward of up to $20 million and possible relocation for information about Iran’s nuclear program, including its facilities, equipment, and associated personnel, such as those in the scientific community,” US Central Command said on X. The program was established in 1984 under the State Department’s national security rewards program to offer money for information that protects American lives and interests. In its statement about the reward, the State Department said Iran’s “lack of compliance with the IAEA (International Atomic Energy Agency) on safeguards obligations has led to the agency’s loss of ‘continuity of knowledge’ regarding Iran’s production and inventory of key components like centrifuges. It gave no specific parameters on what information would yield a $20 million reward. Trump has repeatedly said US forces have effectively obliterated Iran’s nuclear program. “If we didn’t hit Iran, you wouldn’t have Israel today,” Trump said Friday night in West Palm Beach, Florida. “If they had nuclear, they would have used nuclear. They would have obliterated the Middle East.” But the president also said Iran – which he stressed has had its economy and military severely damaged over eight months of war – is eager to end the conflict. “We’re dealing with them now. They want to make a deal very badly,” he said. Diplomatic efforts by mediators have been in full swing in an attempt to prevent any resumption of fighting. And on Tuesday Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian said his government was still trying to resolve the crisis through dialogue. Earlier this week Trump said he still had to “take care” of one or two targets, including so-called Pickaxe Mountain in central Iran, a suspected nuclear site which Tehran denies is such a facility. business.title: U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows The U.S. Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network issued a final order Friday that will cut offshore exchange MEXC Global off from the American banking system over alleged links to sanctions evasion by Iran, North Korea and Russia, the department said . FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says. What the order does — and when The order , signed by FinCEN Deputy Director Jimmy L. Kirby, covers MEXC Global and named affiliates operating outside the United States, including Seychelles-incorporated MEXC Global Ltd / MX Global Ltd, Estonia’s MEXC Estonia OÜ, Switzerland’s GIDA Technology AG and the U.K.’s MXC Global Ltd, plus successors. Covered institutions face civil or criminal penalties for willful violations. Until the Federal Register publishes the notice, the 30-day clock has not started. As of Friday evening eastern time the Register’s public index still showed no MEXC document, matching the order’s own cover note that publication is pending. Background on MEXC Founded in 2018 and formerly branded MXC, MEXC ranks among the world’s 20 largest centralized crypto venues by volume. Treasury puts daily turnover above $1 billion and reserves near $5 billion as of mid-2026, with access claimed across more than 170 countries. The exchange already lists the United States as a prohibited jurisdiction in its user terms, so Friday’s action mainly hits any remaining dollar rails, banking partners and counterparties that still touch U.S. institutions. Regulators elsewhere have been circling for years. The U.K. Financial Conduct Authority put MEXC Global Ltd on its warning list in March 2024 as unauthorized. business.title: Bitcoin Magazine Books Opens 333-Copy Genesis Book Collector Edition for 3rd Anniversary
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Magazine Books Opens 333-Copy Genesis Book Collector Edition for 3rd Anniversary Bitcoin Magazine Books opened a third-anniversary campaign Friday for Aaron van Wirdum’s The Genesis Book , offering a redesigned Collectors Edition limited to 333 hand-signed, individually numbered hardcovers in an exclusive Genesis Block slipcase. Each Collectors Edition hardcover is hand-signed and hand-numbered by van Wirdum, the former Bitcoin Magazine editor-in-chief whose book traces the people, projects and ideas that preceded Satoshi Nakamoto’s peer-to-peer cash design. The standard package is priced at $221 and pairs the book with a limited trading card carrying a Certificate of Authenticity, a collector pin, a sticker sheet, the slipcase and a digital package. Two one-of-one packages sit outside the ordinary number queue. The #1 package is listed at $5,000 and the #21 package at $2,500; each includes the matching numbered copy, a matching one-of-one collector card and the same accessories as the standard collector package. Standard collector numbers are assigned in purchase order starting at #2 and skipping #21, the campaign FAQ says. Once preorders close, the signed Genesis print run will not be reproduced. The Genesis Book Collector's Edition is live! 333 copies. Individually numbered. Exclusive Genesis Block slipcase. Hand-signed by Aaron van Wirdum. Once they're gone, they're gone. pic.twitter.com/BgiJoCVt8m — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 6, 2026 What ships with the anniversary editions Beside the signed run, Bitcoin Magazine Books is selling a Premium Edition hardcover for $160 with foil stamping, a ribbon marker, stained page edges and custom endsheets. That edition is not limited, signed, numbered or slipcased, and it does not include the collector accessories or digital files. A standalone Digital Package at $9.99 delivers the ebook in EPUB and the audiobook in MP4 immediately after purchase, independent of whether the physical campaign clears its funding bar. Physical collector and premium orders are scheduled to ship in calendar year 2027. Van Wirdum , who discovered bitcoin in 2013 and later led Bitcoin Magazine ‘s editorial desk, frames The Genesis Book as a history of computer scientists, privacy activists and heterodox economists who chased government-independent digital money long before the 2008 white paper — from early cypherpunk culture through experiments such as David Chaum’s ecash, Wei Dai’s b-money, Adam Back’s Hashcash and Hal Finney’s reusable proof of work. Store images for the slipcase and accessories are artistic renderings; the campaign page notes that color, materials and finishes may vary in production. The campaign is operated by BTC Inc., which publishes Bitcoin Magazine . business.title: Thailand SEC Files Criminal Complaint Against Bitget Ahead of Dec. 5 Access Block
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Thailand SEC Files Criminal Complaint Against Bitget Ahead of Dec. 5 Access Block Thailand’s Securities and Exchange Commission filed a criminal complaint Thursday against BG Limited, the operator of cryptocurrency exchange Bitget, alleging it ran an unlicensed digital-asset exchange for Thai users from 2022 to 2025, and notified the government to block the platform from Dec. 5. The complaint, lodged with the Economic Crime Suppression Division, also names Mr. Kritsana Kritsananuwat as an alleged supporter who promoted Bitget through Facebook and YouTube channels, the SEC said in statement No. 241/2026. From 2022 through 2025, the regulator found, Bitget offered a trading system in the ordinary course of business, charged fees, ran a Thai-language website that could show values in baht, and solicited Thai users on social channels including “Bitget Thailand” on X, “BGB Thai Holder” on Telegram and “bitgetthailand” on TikTok. That conduct amounts to operating a digital-asset exchange under Section 3 of the Emergency Decree on Digital Asset Businesses B.E. 2561 (2018) without a license, a violation of Section 26 punishable under Section 66, the SEC said. The case now moves to an inquiry official, then prosecutors and the courts. Separately, the SEC submitted Bitget’s website, other domains and its app to the Ministry of Digital Economy and Society under a 2025 royal decree that authorizes access blocks on unlicensed trading platforms. From Dec. 5, the public “will be unable to access the platform,” the statement said, and investors still holding assets there were told to consider acting before the cutoff. A licensed path that now sits next to a criminal case The enforcement push lands weeks after Bitget announced a planned acquisition of GMO-Z.com Cryptonomics (Thailand), a Bangkok digital-asset exchange and brokerage that already holds Thai licenses, through its interest in BTGT Management (Thailand) Ltd. Under that deal, GMO Internet and its Thai holding company would transfer their entire stake in GMO-Z — about 49% and 50.94%, respectively — to BTGT or a designee at completion, a Sept. 24 GMO Internet filing showed. Bitget said completion remains subject to regulatory approval and, after a change-of-control nod, it intends to introduce its trading platform to Thai users under local rules. “Thailand is an important part of Southeast Asia’s digital asset landscape, and this acquisition gives us a great opportunity to establish local operations,” Bitget CEO Gracy Chen said in the Oct. 20 release. The timetable has already slipped. GMO Internet Group pushed the effective date of the share transfer from Oct. 31 to Nov. 30, citing careful work on Thai regulatory applications and closing procedures. That revised date sits five days before the planned Bitget access block. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky, her Spring/Summer 2027 collection , Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis. The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A Cycle Of Giving Back In nature, nothing is wasted and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back.That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. sports.description: Former England captain Michael Vaughan has reacted sarcastically to the fresh revelations surrounding Australia's infamous 2018 ball-tampering scandal, suggesting that Usman Khawaja's claims about widespread knowledge within the team were hardly surprising. Khawaja has reignited the 'Sandpapergate' controversy through excerpts from his upcoming autobiography, claiming that discussions about tampering with the ball were much more widespread during Australia's 2018 tour of South Africa than Cricket Australia's investigation had established. Taking to X, Vaughan took a dig at the revelations, suggesting that the latest claims merely confirmed what many had suspected all along. He also questioned why the issue was being revisited nearly eight years after the scandal and called for everyone to move on. "So we finally now know the most hidden secret in the game … all the Aussie team knew about the sandpaper … 8 yrs later it all comes out … no shit Sherlock … now can we just move on …" Vaughan posted. The controversy dates back to the third Test between Australia and South Africa in Cape Town in March 2018, when Cameron Bancroft was caught using sandpaper to rough up the ball. The incident triggered a major crisis for Australian cricket and resulted in lengthy suspensions for Steve Smith, David Warner and Bancroft. Cricket Australia's investigation at the time concluded that prior knowledge of the ball-tampering plan was limited to the three players. Head coach Darren Lehmann was cleared of direct involvement but resigned shortly after the series. However, Khawaja has now claimed that conversations about roughing up the ball, including through the use of sandpaper, took place openly within the team. "It was all of us," the former Australia batter said in his autobiography, according to the Sydney Morning Herald. Khawaja, who was cleared of wrongdoing during the original investigation, also described the conversations as "open, lighthearted discussions" and maintained that awareness of the subject extended beyond just the batters, bowlers or coaching staff. Cricket Australia has stood by its original investigation, insisting that all relevant information presented to the governing body had been considered. It also maintained that individuals still had the opportunity to provide any additional information. Australia captain Pat Cummins, who featured in the Cape Town Test, had earlier played down suggestions that Khawaja's autobiography would trigger further fallout from the scandal. sports.description: KOLKATA: At 15, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is set for his first assignment as Bihar’s senior team captain, with the selectors handing the teenage batting sensation the reins for the upcoming Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy. The move underlines their faith in his leadership potential as Bihar seek a turnaround after losing all four of their opening Ranji Trophy matches. Sakibul Gani led Bihar in the first three Ranji games before Mangal Mahrour took over against Goa, but neither captain could arrest the slide. The BCCI-appointed selection committee, headed by Harvinder Singh, has now turned to Vaibhav, with Suraj Kashyap named his deputy for the domestic T20 tournament. The decision by the selection committee, led by chief selector Harvinder Singh and comprising Amitabh Vijayvargiya and S Sarath, marks another significant step in Vaibhav’s rapid rise. Having represented Rajasthan Royals in the IPL and made his India debut in T20Is, the teenager has quickly established himself as one of the country’s most exciting batting prospects. His recent international exploits included a 45 off 19 balls against New Zealand in the third T20I, where he shared a record-breaking opening stand with Abhishek Sharma. Vaibhav has also had a taste of leadership at the zonal level. Named vice-captain of the Ishan Kishan-led East Zone side, he briefly took charge during the Duleep Trophy semifinal when Kishan left the field with a finger injury. During that spell, he also successfully executed a DRS call. However, his rapid elevation to positions of responsibility comes amid questions about the need to balance expectations with his development. Sachin Tendulkar recently advocated giving Vaibhav more opportunities in red-ball cricket to help him grow as a complete cricketer, while cautioning against placing excessive responsibility on his young shoulders too early. The selectors, though, appear to have a different assessment, with the Bihar captaincy adding another responsibility to Vaibhav’s expanding portfolio. BCA president Harsh Vardhan said the appointment would provide the youngster another opportunity to develop as a leader. “Vaibhav has already demonstrated tremendous talent, confidence and maturity at a young age, and this responsibility will provide him with another opportunity to grow as a cricketer and leader,” he said. sports.description: Arsenal youth trains with first-team amid senior international call-up Arsenal youngster James Scanlon is having a good week, receiving call-ups to train with the Gunners first-team and to play with Gibraltar over the international break. Arsenal are obviously a little low on wingers at the moment, with Bukayo Saka out of action through injury and Max Dowman suspended. With Scanlon scoring three goals and assisting one in his first five Premier League 2 appearances for the Gunners, he’s earned a chance in training. But that wasn’t the only boost for the former Manchester United winger this week, as he’s also been called up to the Gibraltar senior squad for the November break. Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images The international call-up isn’t surprising, as Scanlon has already made 28 appearances for Gibraltar in his young career. In fact, Scanlon is currently the team’s second-top scorer of all time, with six goals. He only trails retired international Liam Walker , who scored eight during his international career. The Arsenal man will get an opportunity to add to his total in Nations League fixtures away to Andorra and at home to Malta over the upcoming break. sports.description: Stafford Rangers manager Graham Deakin stepped up from his role as coach to take over at Marston Road in February - and save his side from the drop [Stafford Rangers FC] Stafford Rangers go into Sunday's FA Cup first-round tie with promotion-chasing League Two side Grimsby Town as very much the underdogs. They are the lowest-ranked side left in this year's competition. Second in the Northern Premier League West Division, the eighth-tier club will be up against a team from four levels higher - currently standing sixth in League Two. Skip back 50 years and Rangers were ruling the roost in non-league football. Three times they went to Wembley, twice winning the FA Trophy, in 1972 and 1979, under the command of Roy Chapman, father of Leeds United title winner and former Stoke City striker Lee. And, in between, they also reached the fourth round of the FA Cup. Despite being founder members of non-league football's first 'fifth division', the Alliance Premier League, when it launched in 1979, it then all fizzled out as the club went into decline. The average weekly crowds of up to 4,000 dropped off, finances suffered and Rangers lost their way. From the archives: Stafford Rangers on BBC Radio Stoke Rangers did win back their place in the fifth tier briefly in 2006, under Stafford-born former Wolves and Stoke midfielder Phil Robinson. But that lasted just two seasons and he had departed before they went back down again under Wolves legend Steve Bull in 2008. Now Rangers are back up and fighting again - and this cup run has been a major catalyst, encapsulated by the 5-0 fourth qualifying round replay win over Gateshead which got them to this stage. "The feeling we have around the club is one of anticipation," chief executive David Smith told BBC Radio Stoke. "The place is buzzing. "There's people everywhere working, trying to get the ground ready – to make it the way we want to be. "It's quite a challenge for us, to be live on TV on Sunday lunchtime. But the staff have put in many hours of service to be match ready. We've already had three full houses here of 3,000 plus crowds, so we're almost getting used to it." They were also cup giantkillers themselves little more than a year ago when they beat Manchester United on penalties in the EFL Cup. sports.description: Brazil face North Korea seeking first U17 Women's World Cup medal Brazil’s U-17 women’s national team faces another decisive test this Saturday (7). Led by head coach Rilany Silva, the team takes on North Korea at 12 p.m. (Brasília time) in the third-place match of the U-17 Women’s World Cup at the Mohammed VI Women’s Football Complex in Salé, Morocco. At stake is the chance to claim Brazil’s first-ever medal in the competition. technology.title: NHS breach helpline left staff carrying a 'significant emotional burden'
technology.description: NHS staff drafted into a helpline after colleagues' health data was exposed online faced distressed callers, safeguarding concerns, and a "serious emotional impact," a review has found. The report [PDF] comes almost exactly a year after the Royal Cornwall Hospitals NHS Trust disclosed a data breach affecting 8,003 people, including current and former trust staff and non-trust workers. A member of the public discovered the exposure in November 2025. An Excel workbook published in response to a Freedom of Information request in February 2023 retained underlying sickness absence records that users could reveal through its pivot tables. Staff assigned to the helpline described difficult calls involving shouting, anger, and distress. Particularly difficult calls involved people distressed by the sensitivity of the disclosures or potentially in danger from domestic abuse. Call handlers said they had to make safeguarding assessments without training or an established process. "Such occurrences of anger or distress were not infrequent, and this reflected the heightened emotions and distress experienced by callers to varying degrees due to the breach," the review noted. "This placed significant emotional burden on individuals working in the contact center, who were not prepared or provided support on how to deal with those." Members of the trust's clinical governance team were told just a day beforehand that they would staff the helpline. Despite their experience dealing with patient trauma, they received little preparation for the calls that followed. "The staff working in the call centers had a short training session and then the calls started coming in within minutes of the team being set up," the review noted. "Some staff had not finished reading the pre-prepared script which had arrived only 30 minutes before the center went live." Most call handlers only learned that their own data had been exposed while already working on the helpline, sometimes minutes before supporting others affected. Call handlers also said they had little choice about taking on the work and were expected to maintain their usual duties alongside it. The review stated that some staff members gave up weekends and worked long past their scheduled hours to meet the demands of both roles. "It's typical NHS, it runs on goodwill," one staffer told the team that compiled the report. The call center was only supposed to run for two weeks in December 2025, but due to the volume of calls, it was eventually stood down after 11 weeks, in February 2026. According to officials speaking at a trust board meeting on Thursday, the review and its findings have since been circulated among staff, and published online. technology.title: The datacentre arms race hits pause in south-east Asia
technology.description: Power and water constraints are pressuring what seemed like a juggernaut of growth for the region just months ago In early 2026, Thailand’s datacentre industry was on a roll. As the year has passed, however, what once seemed like a new industrial juggernaut has ground to a halt.
